title: Function-call & schema compatibility guard for rollouts
creator: Priya Shah
description: Add a compatibility guard that validates structured output (JSON + function-call contracts) during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts and triggers automated mitigation (alerts, pause, rollback) if the new model diverges from the pinned contract. This work spans runtime API checks, rollout orchestration logic, telemetry, and a lightweight diffing engine that quantifies function-call and schema deltas. The goal is to prevent silent breakage of tool-calling integrations and downstream consumers when a newly promoted model changes function names, parameter lists, or expected return shapes.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility guard can be toggled per-rollout and per-route in the Console
During shadow traffic, the guard records function-call diffs and schema validation failures to the rollout trace events and increases severity when required fields are missing

Canary traffic (configurable pct) is automatically paused and a rollback is triggered when schema_validation_failure_rate > 1% over a 30m window OR critical function signature drift is detected (new required param removed or return type incompatible)
A human-readable diff is attached to the rollout UI and included in alert payloads and Slack notifications
Integration tests (unit + e2e harness) covering common drift cases (param removed/renamed, nested object type change, optional -> required) pass in CI
Telemetry metrics emitted: schema_validation_failure_rate, function_signature_variants, function_call_mismatch_rate, and signature_change_entropy
Docs and runbook describing thresholds, how to interpret diffs, and manual override steps are published (Confluence link in task).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Shadow-only collection (100% shadow) for 48h against golden prompt set to collect baseline diffs; never serves user-facing responses
Phase 1: Canary 1% for 24h with guard active in 'observe' mode (does not auto-pause) to validate false-positive rate
Phase 2: Canary 5% for 48h with guard active in 'enforce' mode (auto-pause + notify) if thresholds hit
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 20% then 100% with rolling windows and daily checkpoints; auto-rollback enabled by default for production routes
Fallbacks: route to previous model variant or lower-cost compatible variant when paused/rolled back
telemetry_and_metrics: schema_validation_failure_rate: fraction of responses failing JSON schema or missing required function fields
function_call_mismatch_rate: fraction where the function name or parameter set differs from pinned contract
function_signature_variants: cardinality of observed signatures per function over window
signature_change_entropy: measure of dispersion of signature changes (used to detect noisy nondeterministic changes)
latency_p50/p95 change tied to rollout (to detect perf regressions caused by guard)
tests: Unit: schema comparator library tests for nested validation, type coercion, required/optional transitions
Fuzz: generate random function-call payloads to assert guard doesn't crash runtime
E2E: rollout-harness executes golden prompt set and asserts no auto-rollback for allowed changes and rollback for disallowed changes
Integration: ensure telemetry events show up on console dashboards and PagerDuty alerts trigger when thresholds exceeded
risks: False positives from schema validation could unnecessarily rollback models if thresholds are too strict (mitigate by phased observe mode)
Increased latency for responses that need on-the-fly validation; must measure and bound overhead (<10ms target)
Guard complexity could increase operational burden for teams using flexible/loosely-typed tool contracts
Edge cases: models emitting new function wrappers (e.g., dynamic function naming) require mapping rules to avoid noise
